title: Staged enablement plan: Auto-rollback on SLO breach (feature rollout plan)
content:
Doc owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Last reviewed with: Sean Gallagher (SRE), Jada Williams (Rollout Controller), Chloe Martin (Console), Aisha Bello (Obs)

Purpose
Enable the “auto-rollback on SLO breach” capability safely across environments and regions. This plan covers the feature rollout (not customer model rollouts), including required gates, sequencing (pause-only -> rollback), internal canary services, region-by-region enablement, and explicit backout criteria.

Scope of this enablement plan
- Feature: rollout controller integrates with SLO monitors and can take automatic actions (pause / rollback / shift traffic) based on configured policy.
- Environments: dev -> staging -> prod.
- Modes: Hosted API first, then Dedicated (reserved capacity), then Private control planes (VPC/on-prem) gated separately.
- Actions: Phase 1 is “auto-pause only”; Phase 2 adds “auto-rollback” for canary/A-B traffic splits.
- Non-goals: multi-region failover orchestration; eval/quality-based rollback.

Definitions
- “Auto action”: a controller-issued action such as pause rollout step, rollback to baseline model/version, or suppress (with justification).
- “Breach”: SLO breach per ADR-0127 (fast/slow burn windows + debounce + minimum sample gating).
- “Monitor freshness”: monitor data not older than the staleness threshold; missing/stale is treated per policy defaults (see below).

Feature flags and kill switches
We will roll out behind explicit, layered controls so we can back out quickly without code rollback:
1) Global master kill switch (highest priority)
   - Flag: rollouts.slo_auto_actions.master_enabled
   - Default: OFF in all envs; any ON requires Release Eng + SRE sign-off.

2) Environment gating
   - Flag: rollouts.slo_auto_actions.enabled_in_env.<dev|staging|prod>
   - Default: dev ON (after initial validation), staging OFF -> ON, prod OFF -> ON.

3) Action gating (pause vs rollback)
   - Flag: rollouts.slo_auto_actions.action_mode
   - Values: disabled | pause_only | pause_and_rollback
   - Default: disabled (until staged enablement); in prod we will start at pause_only.

4) Scope gating
   - Allowlist: rollouts.slo_auto_actions.allowlist (service/route + region + customer tier)
   - Default: empty allowlist in staging/prod until canary is selected.

5) Policy/config service gating
   - Enforce safe bounds (per policy engine validation): maximum rollback frequency, holdoff/debounce windows, min sample size floors.
   - Any policy changes require a policy version bump and are audited.

Operational note
- Backout is always “flip flags OFF / change action_mode to disabled” first; code rollback is last resort.

Prerequisites (hard gates before enabling outside dev)
A) Observability readiness
- Dashboards live (observability-pack/pr-913) and access verified for oncall groups.
- Alerts configured and routed appropriately:
  - “auto-rollback triggered” (notify, not page initially)
  - “rollback suppressed” (notify)
  - “monitor missing/stale” (page only if systemic; notify if scoped)
- Metrics emitted and labeled per standard (pr-28471), with cardinality checks passed.

B) Audit trail and console readiness
- Audit events emitted to event stream (pr-28435) and visible in Console timeline (Console API + UI work as applicable).
- Required audit fields present (per ADR-0128): policy_version, monitor_ids, decision_trace/correlation_id, metrics snapshot reference.

C) SLO monitor coverage
- For each canary service/route, monitors must exist for:
  - latency p95 and/or p99 (route-scoped)
  - error rate (5xx/timeout at gateway or service)
  - saturation (optional; only where signal is stable)
- Staleness handling confirmed with SRE: monitor “missing/stale” should default to NO auto-rollback (fail-open), but should create a distinct event + alert so humans can remediate coverage.

D) Test readiness
- Staging E2E tests passing (pr-28490): synthetic signal injection for latency + 5xx + monitor staleness.
- Race/idempotency checks landed (pr-28502) for safe rollback execution.

E) Oncall/runbook readiness
- Runbook published in Confluence and linked from dashboard panels.
- Incident-bot notification formatting reviewed (incident-bot/pr-477); ensure it will not create paging storms.

Canary selection (initial)
We want canaries with (1) stable traffic volume, (2) good monitor coverage, (3) low blast radius, (4) owners who can respond quickly.

Staging canary candidates (choose 1–2):
- Hosted API: /v1/chat/completions (internal tenant only)
- Hosted API: /v1/embeddings (internal batch job tenant)

Prod canary candidates (choose 1):
- Hosted API: /v1/chat/completions for Redwood internal dogfood tenant (single region first)
- Dedicated: one internal “Dedicated sandbox” cluster (us-west-2) if available; otherwise defer Dedicated enablement

We will not start with external enterprise tenants in prod. We will graduate to “self-serve low tier” only after we have at least one week of clean internal prod canary data.

Enablement phases and timeline (target)
Dates are indicative; actual cutover happens during release train windows and after SRE sign-off.

Phase 0: Dev validation (Week 0)
Goal: ensure end-to-end wiring is correct and safe under chaos testing without impacting real customers.
- Enable flags in dev:
  - master_enabled=ON
  - enabled_in_env.dev=ON
  - action_mode=pause_only
  - allowlist=dev test services only
- Validate:
  - decision trace correctness (burn-rate windows + debounce + min sample)
  - controller behavior when monitor is missing/stale (no auto action; emits event)
  - audit log schema fields and console surfaces
- Exit criteria:
  - No unbounded flapping in synthetic tests
  - Idempotent behavior under repeated triggers

Phase 1: Staging enablement (Week 1)
Goal: validate in realistic infra with E2E tests and controlled canary rollouts.
Step 1 (staging, pause-only):
- Change flags:
  - master_enabled=ON
  - enabled_in_env.staging=ON
  - action_mode=pause_only
  - allowlist = {one staging canary route + region}
- Run at least two staged rollouts in staging:
  - One where we inject a latency regression (should pause within expected fast burn window)
  - One where we inject transient blip (should not pause due to debounce/min sample)
- Validate Slack notifications (incident-bot) are informative and not noisy.

Step 2 (staging, rollback enabled):
- Change action_mode=pause_and_rollback for same allowlist.
- Execute a canary rollout with forced error-rate breach and verify:
  - rollback executor returns traffic split to baseline safely (rate-limited step down)
  - rollback is idempotent (no double rollback)
  - audit trail includes metrics snapshot references

Exit criteria for staging:
- 0 critical bugs (crash loops, stuck rollouts, repeated actions)
- <2% false positives in synthetic scenarios (as defined by test harness) and none in “transient blip” scenario
- No monitoring gaps for chosen canary scope

Phase 2: Prod internal canary (Week 2)
Goal: minimal blast radius, real traffic, confirm alerting and operational workflow.

Step 1 (prod, pause-only, single region):
- Flags:
  - master_enabled=ON
  - enabled_in_env.prod=ON
  - action_mode=pause_only
  - allowlist = {internal dogfood tenant route + us-east-1 (or us-west-2)}
- Alert routing:
  - “auto action taken” = notify #eng-oncall + #eng-platform (no paging)
  - “monitor stale/missing” = notify; page only if >N services affected or >X minutes
- Run one planned model rollout on the canary route.

Step 2 (prod, rollback enabled, still internal, single region):
- Change action_mode=pause_and_rollback for the same allowlist.
- Confirm rollback behavior via a planned “game day” regression (if feasible) or a controlled synthetic signal injection in prod-like canary stack (preferred).

Exit criteria for internal prod canary:
- At least 7 days without operational incidents caused by the feature (e.g., unwanted rollbacks, stuck state machine)
- At least 1 successful auto action (pause or rollback) in controlled exercise OR strong evidence from staging + controller logs that trigger path is healthy
- Audit and dashboard links used successfully by oncall (tabletop run-through)

Phase 3: Prod gradual expansion (Week 3+)
Goal: expand scope with clear guardrails and rollback limits.

Expansion order (Hosted API):
1) Additional region(s) for internal tenant
2) Self-serve tier (low-risk routes first: embeddings, rerank) in one region
3) Self-serve chat in one region
4) Broader regions (region-by-region)

Region-by-region order (proposed)
- us-east-1 -> us-west-2 -> eu-central-1 -> eu-west-1 -> ap-southeast-1
Rationale: expand from highest operational familiarity and monitor maturity to newer regions.

Dedicated enablement (separate gate)
- Only after Hosted API expansion step (2) is stable.
- Require dedicated-specific saturation signals and distinct allowlist by cluster.

Private enablement (separate gate)
- Opt-in only; require customer environment validation and explicit contract/SLA alignment.
- Default remains OFF unless customer explicitly enables and monitor coverage is confirmed.

Default policy templates (what we ship vs what we enable)
We will ship policy templates in the policy editor, but they will not be active unless allowlisted.
- Template: “Conservative (pause-only)”
  - burn windows: fast 5m + slow 30m
  - min sample: per tier floor (SRE guidance)
  - actions: pause only
- Template: “Standard (pause + rollback)”
  - same windows, with rollback enabled after holdoff
  - max 1 rollback per rollout per 60m (guardrail)
- Template: “Aggressive (internal only)”
  - only available for internal tenants; not enabled in prod external by default

Backout plan (must be executable in <5 minutes)
Primary backout (no code rollback):
1) Set rollouts.slo_auto_actions.action_mode=disabled
2) If still unsafe, set rollouts.slo_auto_actions.master_enabled=OFF
3) Clear allowlist (defense in depth)
4) If required, disable incident-bot auto-rollback notifications (to reduce noise while stabilizing)

Secondary backout (policy level):
- Revert policy template defaults to pause_only and/or increase min sample thresholds.
- Add temporary suppression window for affected service/route (admin-only override) with justification.

Tertiary backout (code rollback):
- Roll back the rollout controller deploy to previous release train build. This is last resort; use only if flags do not prevent actions or if controller is unstable.

Backout criteria (trigger conditions)
Any of the following triggers an immediate backout to action_mode=disabled in the affected environment:
- Unintended rollback affecting external customer traffic (P0)
- Controller enters stuck state (rollout cannot proceed/rollback) for >10 minutes in prod
- Repeated actions (pause/rollback) for same rollout step indicating flapping despite debounce (more than 2 actions within 30 minutes)
- Monitor missing/stale causes actions (should never happen; indicates bug)
- Alert noise: >10 notifications/hour across org due to this feature (evaluate; disable if needed)

Comms plan
- Pre-enable announcement (internal): #announcements + #eng-platform with:
  - what is being enabled (pause-only first)
  - where to see events (dashboard + Console timeline)
  - how to request opt-in (service owners)
- During staging/prod canary: daily status update in #eng-releases thread
- Post expansion step: short retro note with metrics (actions taken, false positives, time-to-rollback)

Ownership / approvals
- Required approvals to enable prod flags:
  - Release Eng (Connor O’Brien)
  - SRE sign-off (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes)
  - Rollout controller owner (Jada Williams)
- Observability readiness sign-off:
  - Aisha Bello (alerts/dashboards)

Runbook hooks (what oncall does when it fires)
- If auto action triggers:
  - Confirm scope (rollout id, route, model version, region, tier)
  - Validate monitor freshness and sample size
  - Check if known incident/suppression should apply
  - Decide whether to keep paused, rollback, or manually mitigate
- If monitor missing/stale event triggers:
  - Treat as coverage gap: no auto action should happen; file follow-up to add/repair monitor; do not broaden allowlist until resolved

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm final canary route(s) and internal tenant identifiers (need Console + Platform alignment).
- Confirm exact region order based on current monitor maturity (use the SLO coverage audit sheet).
- Decide whether initial prod rollback enablement requires a planned game day vs “staging evidence only”.
- Confirm paging policy for “rollback failed” vs “rollback triggered” (likely page only on failed execution / stuck rollout).

Change log
- 2026-02-20: initial draft created (release train notes thread)
- 2026-02-24: added explicit pause-only -> rollback sequencing and region order
- 2026-02-27: tightened backout criteria + prerequisites; aligned with ADR-0127/0128 and dashboard PR-913
